newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai govt mulls cutting soymeal tariff to 5 pct.
newsitem.headline: Thai govt mulls cutting soymeal tariff to 5 pct.

text.p: The Thai cabinet will consider on Tuesday a proposal to cut the soymeal tariff to five percent from the current 10 percent, a commerce ministry official told Reuters.
"The commerce ministry proposed a five percent cut. But it is up to the cabinet to decide on the appropriate level," the official told Reuters.
The move to cut soymeal tariffs came after the feed industry urged the government to remove the 10 percent import duty on soymeal, saying the soaring prices of soymeal has driven up production costs.
But the commerce ministry agreed only to cut the tariff to five percent. It said the removal of the soymeal tariff could affect the oil crushing business.

Since vegetable oil is a price-controlled product, the government allows the crushers to import soybeans tariff-free. The industry makes a profit to offset the low vegetable oil prices by selling by-product soymeal.
